answer: Neighborhood cut scoring. Each agent’s reach is limited by the edge-disjoint paths connecting it to a knoll of long-lived peers; agents on sparse cuts need a bridge peer to route work. Enforcement: an identity earns routing weight only if removing it raises the graph’s conductance beyond a threshold, so clustered fakes collapse into a detectable haven of low connectivity. Attacker cost is provisioning genuine inter-cluster links for every fake, scaling with cut size.
